title: Spreadsheets and financial models
acceptance: Complete draft delivered for root's independent review and prerequisite-ordered acceptance; this agent has not changed canonical chapter acceptance or shared production state.
scope: Cell addresses, formulas, relative/absolute/mixed references and formula-copy intent
Cash-flow signs, time-zero versus end-of-period timing, rate/unit conventions and economic model boundary
Explicit working-capital and equipment timelines, independent net-present-value calculation routes and rounding
Bank reconciliation, independently sourced target, supported corrections and offsetting-error counterexamples
Formula-based two-input sensitivity table, conditional break-even threshold and scenario limitations
Input validation, formula inspection, tolerances, perturbation tests, provenance and remaining model risk

checks.arithmetic: Independent Fraction-based direct discount powers verify all four-date cash flows, present values, the shifted-time-zero mistake, rounding discrepancy, nine sensitivity cells, slope/intercept and quantity break-even. Gross receipts/payment identities verify two bank reconciliations and offsetting mistakes. All determinate exercise values were recomputed, including a missing zero period, partial working-capital recovery, reduced disposal proceeds, effective annual/monthly rates, capex change, cash-flow delay and zero rate.
checks.reasoning: Audited signs and units; time zero stays undiscounted and periodic NPV starts at t=1. Working capital is distinct from operating cash and released only under an explicit recovery assumption. Reconciliation residual sign and independent-target requirement are stated; passing a net identity does not prove gross-flow accuracy. Sensitivity slope is positive because margin is positive; the threshold is conditional and supplies no probabilities. Discount-rate monotonicity is restricted to nonnegative future cash flows. Cash flows exclude taxes and financing under a stated teaching boundary; no real investment recommendation is inferred.
checks.solutions: All eight prompts have matching solutions. Exercises 1–6 and 8 include complete reference translations or determinate calculations; Exercises 7–8 give concrete evaluation criteria and example reasoning for open audit/evidence questions. The delayed net operating cash flow is explicitly distinguished from gross receipts. All exercise methods are introduced before use.
checks.sources: Inspected the two exact official Microsoft routes recorded in v04-c02-sources.json. Used reference-copy and NPV function conventions accurately. The reference page contains an incidental prose direction error; the manuscript follows the correctly stated coordinate definitions/table. Source claims are scoped to software syntax, not validation of economic forecasts. All numerical examples and synthetic inputs are authored for this chapter.
checks.instruction: Introduces workbook/cell/formula/range/format meanings before references; establishes timelines and units before NPV; supplies a full input and formula map before sensitivity copying. Covers absent/zero values, intermediate rounding, partial recovery, zero/negative-rate boundaries and interpretive limits. Includes a practical model/audit-log deliverable, teach-back, delayed check and successor link.
checks.structure: Own checker confirms an HTML fragment with no h1, two worked-example asides, eight exercise and eight solution list items, required retention prompts, exact source IDs and existing project files. The sensitivity expression is extracted from the actual manuscript, copied with a restricted A1 translator, and evaluated by a safe arithmetic interpreter against a separately derived exact revenue/payment decomposition. Source package links use flat dist-root filenames as required by build.py. Central build, cross-reference acceptance and full-library verification belong to root.

verification_commands.coverage: Seven grouped structural, formula, exact-arithmetic and benchmark/invalid-input checks; check() returns a dict with status, checks and limitations.
Offline JSON output includes complete base timeline, nine sensitivity cells, bank residual before and after correction, input provenance and limitations.

limitations: This is agent author review, not independent academic certification, human expert review or learner testing. Root acceptance remains pending.

Formula-map review, a restricted arithmetic/reference interpreter and an independent Python benchmark are not a real spreadsheet application's recalculation test. No Excel, LibreOffice or other workbook engine, GUI, formula cache or application-specific settings were tested; no workbook file is supplied or requested.

The benchmark intentionally supports exactly three annual periods, nonnegative quantity and payment-magnitude inputs, finite rates greater than -1, and the stated synthetic cash-flow boundary. It is a teaching implementation, not a general valuation engine.
The numeric checker verifies the examples and solutions, not empirical plausibility of input forecasts or appropriate discount rates. Independent implementations can share a flawed assumption.
Browser visual/mobile/print UI QA remains pending because the earlier local-file browser attempt was blocked by security policy. No browser workaround was attempted.
Central build, all-library offline links and integration of source identifiers must still be performed by root after prerequisite review.
